A Trusted East Harlem Vet That Truly Cares: Why Oliver’s Dog and Cat Clinic Is a Hidden Gem in NYC

After my dear, longtime vet passed away and several disastrous visits to BondVet left me frustrated, anxious, and honestly a little traumatized, I wasn’t sure where to turn. In a city full of clinics, finding a vet who is skilled, compassionate, and actually reachable can feel like chasing a mythical trifecta. But then I found Oliver’s Dog and Cat Clinic in East Harlem, and that impossible balance suddenly felt refreshingly real.

I brought in my cat, JoJo, for a neutering procedure—at age three. I knew it should’ve happened earlier, but after my experience with BondVet, I’d been hesitant and nervous to trust again. Dr. Coronato didn’t judge, didn’t lecture, and didn’t make me feel bad. She was kind, understanding, and fully focused on making sure JoJo was safe and cared for.

She’s chill, funny, and genuinely excellent at what she does. She explained everything clearly, handled JoJo with gentleness, and made what could’ve been a stressful situation feel easy. After the surgery, she personally called to check in on JoJo, and when I had a question the next day, she picked up the phone herself. That kind of follow-through is rare—especially in NYC.

Even though Oliver’s Dog and Cat Clinic is a small practice, it’s impressively well-equipped. They offer in-house diagnostics, laser surgery, dental care, X-rays, vaccinations, senior care, pain management, and more. It’s the best of both worlds: the capabilities of a big clinic, with the heart and attention of a small, neighborhood practice.

Big love also to her assistant, who clearly has a natural way with animals—JoJo was completely at ease.

If you’re looking for a trustworthy, non-judgmental vet in East Harlem or anywhere in NYC, look no further. I finally feel like I have a vet I can rely on again—and JoJo agrees.

If zero stars was an option, it would be my rating. After nearly a decade as a client of Dr. Coronato, I feel compelled to share my deeply troubling experience. Although I once overlooked her brusque bedside manner, her recent conduct has been shocking and has caused me significant distress.

I have spent months trying to resolve major errors in my pets’ medical records, which led to incorrect health assessments. My persistent, good-faith efforts to communicate and get these issues fixed have been met not with professionalism, but with what I can only describe as a complete lack of empathy from Dr. Coronato.

The most alarming part of this ordeal was my direct interaction with her. During a recorded phone call, I was stunned by her response to my concerns. Instead of demonstrating the care and responsibility one would expect from a veterinarian, her reaction felt unprofessional and dismissive.

What is especially telling is that, despite failing to reply to my repeated emails requesting corrections to my pets' medical records, Dr. Coronato did manage to promptly fix the misspelling of her own name on the clinic’s website—a mistake I had brought to her attention in those very same emails. It is clear where her priorities lie.

This situation has had a significant financial and emotional impact on me, even forcing me to seek legal help in addition to paying over $1,000 in vet bills. It's disheartening to see such a long-term relationship end this way, especially when all I wanted was accurate records for my pets. Based on this experience, I cannot recommend Dr. Coronato. Pet owners deserve a veterinarian who responds to legitimate concerns with compassion and professionalism, not dismissiveness.
